applied: HIGH (Spec Reference Deviation 1 + AC3 + Technical Notes 'Ordering against the reaper') — the story's headline correction of DF3.7 was itself factually wrong. It claimed the unattended run 'does not bill forever; it is silently collected at 4 h'. Verified: the reaper has no scheduler. Its only entry point is the operator CLI scripts/sandbox-reap.ts, which is DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT and mutates only under --yes (sandbox-reap.ts:5-9, :50-51), and staleAfterMs is a threshold applied at whatever moment a sweep runs (reaper.ts:459 `aged`), never a clock that fires. So DF3.7's 'bills until an operator acts' sentence STANDS and must not be corrected. What is genuinely wrong in DF3.7 is the ARM: it cites record-claim-refused (reaper.ts:750-756), which guards destroy only, whereas an aged OPEN record classifies stale-record -> teardown (:480-487 VM-side, :534-544 record-side) and teardownSandbox is called with no opts (:671) — harvest, destroy, revoke, closedAt, and no reverify(). Rewrote Deviation 1 to correct the arm and the lost WITNESS while explicitly declining to correct the billing claim; rewrote the restatement in Technical Notes to match.

HIGH (AC3, follow-on) — 'It wins the race by being scheduled inside the ceiling' was an unsupported correctness argument: there is no scheduled reaper to outrun. Rewrote AC3 as 'the guarantee is the refusal, not the interval' — the staleAfterMs-derived interval reduces exposure and is documented as the heuristic it is, and may not be stated as winning a race; the load-bearing clause is the completion-unwitnessed refusal when it loses. Trigger Surface row 'the sweep beats the ceiling instead' corrected to match.

HIGH (AC2b / Files to Modify / Region ownership) — the story specified that src/fleet/run-completion.ts (DF3.7's module) 'adds only the run-lock acquisition around the chain composition'. That edit breaks the sibling's shipped path. Verified: acquireRunLock is explicitly NOT re-entrant and throws a dedicated RunLockReentrantError on a same-process second acquire (scripts/lib/run-lock.ts:64-77, guard at :951 `if (moduleState().held.has(lock)) throw`), and fleet dispatch already holds that same per-run lock for its whole invocation (scripts/fleet.ts:1760-1766 dispatchLock, taken at :1908), which is exactly where DF3.7's --await-completion observer and chain run. An acquisition inside the shared composition would refuse DF3.7's own foreground path with run-lock-reentrant. Moved the acquisition into src/fleet/observe.ts (this story's own module); run-completion.ts gains only a LOCK-AGNOSTIC re-entrant entry point called with the lock already held. Same edit propagated to Files to Modify, Region ownership, INV-IBOX-17 and two DoD boxes, with a new negative control.

HIGH (AC2c, the two-observer race) — 'who wins, provably?' had no answer beyond 'a refused lock is a counted skip'. Now decided by construction and cited: the live foreground --await-completion observer wins because the dispatch invocation holds the run lock; the sweep loses at acquireRunLock with RunLockedError -> DF3.1's exit 5. Added the one honest residue: dispatch's own acquisition is deliberately NON-FATAL on refusal (scripts/fleet.ts:1905-1918, 'a refusal here must NOT abort the mint'), so in that window the foreground chain runs unlocked and the exclusion degrades to the F106 residue DF3.7 documented — narrowed, not closed.

HIGH (AC4a, the reboot arithmetic is inverted) — the story counted box_reboot_after_dispatch 'when the derived boot time postdates the record's createdAt'. Verified that store.create (which stamps createdAt) runs BEFORE driver.create() boots the VM (src/fleet/dispatch.ts:2787-2788, 'the record exists WITHOUT a requestId — for the whole of driver.create()'), so a first boot ALWAYS postdates createdAt and the stated rule counts EVERY healthy box as rebooted — tripping the named 2-event threshold on the second observation and reopening an ADR decision on pure noise. Replaced with the duration form `uptimeSeconds < (hostNow - createdAt) - PROVISION_LAG_MARGIN_MS`, which also removes host/box clock skew from the comparison entirely (uptime is a duration; both remaining terms are host-stamped). Added the margin as a named minted bound and a negative control that fails the naive comparison; DoD AC4 box rewritten to assert the never-rebooted box counts ZERO.

HIGH (User Story / Overview / Wiring closed / INV-IBOX-19 — the product claim vs the mechanism) — the user story opened with 'closed the laptop' and the delivered mechanism is a cron/launchd entry ON THAT LAPTOP, which runs no tick while the machine is off. The story never confronted this. Added an explicit 'What this does not deliver' paragraph to the Overview, retargeted the user story onto 'the host coming BACK, not staying UP', bounded the Wiring-closed claim to 'the first host invocation after it settles', and rewrote INV-IBOX-19 to say plainly that nothing supervises the host watcher and nothing is claimed to. Also noted in the rejected-alternatives entry that a resident host watcher buys nothing on this case either.

HIGH (AC5 / INV-IBOX-17 / Spec Reference — INV-IBOX-16 was quoted selectively) — the story asserted DF3.7's INV-IBOX-16 was 'preserved literally, not narrowed', quoting it as '(no watcher process, no second expiry clock, no persisted field)'. DF3.7's actual invariant is titled 'one reverify entry, no daemon, no new state' and its load-bearing clause reads 'the observer is the only automatic caller of the host chain ... the invariant is no new automatic caller'. DF3.8 IS a new automatic caller; INV-IBOX-17's title ('scheduling is not a second entry') redefined the very word DF3.7 used to draw the line. Rewrote AC5 to split the invariant into its three limbs, preserve two literally, and OPENLY amend the third — the story becomes the second automatic caller and pays for it with the per-run mutex DF3.7 declined to take, trading 'one caller by convention' for 'one caller at a time by mutex', which is strictly stronger for worktree.ts:319's precondition. INV-IBOX-17 retitled 'a second automatic caller, and the mutex that pays for it'; Spec Reference line 9 corrected; AC1's 'no second automatic entry' disambiguated to 'entry point' vs caller.

MEDIUM (AC2d / Technical Notes Contracts) — the story claimed persisting nothing 'keeps a crashed sweep from leaving a lie behind', but a SIGKILLed sweep leaves the run-lock file it took, and treating every RunLockedError as a benign 'another verb owns it, retry next tick' hides a permanently wedged run behind a counted skip forever. RunLockedError already distinguishes the dead-holder case and carries the rm remediation (scripts/lib/run-lock.ts:57-64). Added AC2(d) making a stale refusal its own named, remediated outcome, a third negative control, and the honest exception in the Contracts/Schema note.

MEDIUM (AC4c / INV-IBOX-19 — the threshold had no denominator and no reader) — box_reboot_after_dispatch is emitted per sweep and nothing is persisted, so one rebooted box re-counts on every tick; '2 events' would trip on the second observation of a single box. Defined the counter as per distinct runId and the threshold over DISTINCT runIds across the accumulated evidence set, and named an owner and review point (arc owner, arc retro) so the trigger is not a number in a file nobody reads — which is precisely the failure mode the story indicts DF3.7 for.

MEDIUM (Technical Notes Guards) — one sentence claimed 'the story mints no new ceiling of its own' and the next sentence minted a max-candidates-per-pass. Rewrote as 'every bound but two is inherited', named both minted bounds (PROVISION_LAG_MARGIN_MS and max-candidates-per-pass), and closed the starvation hole the cap opens: enumeration is oldest-createdAt-first and the partial-pass line names the count left behind, since a driven run leaves the candidate set but a permanently refusing one does not.

MEDIUM (Dependency edges / AC7 / DoD e2e) — edges listed DF3.1, DF3.7, DF2.6 while AC7, the E2E Slice and Wiring-closed all require DF1.10's in-box engine, and the detachment AC7 demands is only producible by DF1.10's `fleet run <run-id>` (start the per-run systemd unit and return, DF1.10 AC1). Added DF1.10 as a direct edge with that reasoning, named the mechanism in AC7 and the DoD e2e box, and added DF3.7's scheduling caveat verbatim in kind (no real engine yet => no marker not planted by a test, and a planted marker is not evidence for this AC).

MEDIUM (INV-IBOX-17 — DF3.7's honesty residue was dropped) — DF3.7 was scrupulous that its guard is 'a cheap pre-flight refusal, not a mutual exclusion' and that a hand-run scripts/reverify.ts stays unfenced with F106 left as DF5.1 scoped it. DF3.8's INV-IBOX-17 said only 'Serialization is real, not asserted', which reads as having closed F106. Added the explicit non-fence: the run lock does not cover a hand-run scripts/reverify.ts (it takes no run lock), nor the window where dispatch's own non-fatal acquisition failed — F106 is narrowed, not retired.

LOW (citation drift) — reaper.ts:670 corrected to :671 (the teardownSandbox call; :670 is the wasClosed probe); :749-756 corrected to :750-756 (:749 closes the preceding ownership-recheck-refused push); :524-543 split into the accurate :480-487 (VM-side) and :534-544 (record-side) stale-record rows.

LOW (AC5) — 'the sweep reads DF2.6's ceiling and DF3.4's expiresAt, and owns neither' was vacuous on the second half: a candidate is by definition a record with no approval extension, so no expiresAt exists to read. Corrected in place.

LOW (Technical Notes /proc/uptime) — PROVISION_LAG_MARGIN_MS was introduced with no measured basis, which R10 §7 item 4 forbids ('cite measurements, never folklore'; the arc exists because of a fabricated citation). Recorded it as an OPEN MEASUREMENT: the probe carries no provisioning-to-first-boot duration, the margin is set from the first live e2e's observed lag with a stated multiple, and the evidence JSON carries the raw per-box `(hostNow - createdAt) - uptimeSeconds` so it can be re-derived from data rather than re-argued.

surviving.summary: Arc-level, not fixable inside 4 SP: the schedule runs on the operator's own machine, so reaching the pause still depends on that machine being awake to run a tick. This story removes the requirement that the host stay attached FOR THE DURATION OF THE RUN — which is the real gap DF3.7 left and is worth 4 SP — but the ADR's product claim at :101-102 ('runs that survive host disconnect') is delivered only in the box, not in the host leg. The story now states this bound explicitly in the Overview and INV-IBOX-19 rather than implying otherwise. Operator decision (a hosted/always-on scheduler is a different story), not a spec defect.

DF3.8 is now blocked on two one-clause edits to DF3.7, which is FINAL. Both are recorded in cross_boundary_notes and neither was applied here. Until they land, DF3.7's text and DF3.8's AC5/Deviation 1 disagree on the record — deliberately visible rather than silently reinterpreted, but it is an open cross-story inconsistency, not a closed one.

Scheduling risk, now stacked two deep: AC7's mandatory e2e needs DF3.7 merged (its chain and entry point) AND DF1.10 merged (real in-box engine on a re-pinned image, plus `fleet run` for the detachment). DF3.8 is the last of five in v5-S3 and cannot be verified in parallel with either. The story states the caveat honestly and bars a planted marker as evidence, so the exposure is calendar, not integrity.

Trigger Surface has no in-scope row for the reboot counter (AC4) or the reaper-collected/completion-unwitnessed arm (AC3); all three in-scope rows point at tests/fleet/observe.test.ts, which does cover them per Files to Modify. Table-coverage gap only; the normative statements are complete.

src/reverify/worktree.ts:319 is inherited verbatim from DF3.7 (and from R9 §4 before it) and lands inside the `fire` closure's comment block rather than on the pid-guard baseline computation the F106 note actually depends on. The surrounding block is right and the claim is real; the line number is approximate. Fixing it in DF3.8 alone would desync the two stories, so it is left matching the sibling.

auth-invariants: FIRED — 'Capability gate runs before any side effect': the domain analogue is DF3.7 AC5's approval-extension pre-flight, and the story's whole AC2 exists to force it AFTER lock acquisition and BEFORE any chain step. Satisfiable from the spec alone, with a negative control.

FIRED — 'Resource ownership re-verified per request': the sweep re-reads the extension inside the lock rather than trusting the enumeration-time read; matches the repo's own check-then-act reasoning at scripts/fleet.ts:3852-3855 ('the probe above is deliberately not trusted across the lock boundary').
FIRED — 'Negative-auth test per endpoint': every AC carries at least one MUST-fail negative control and each maps to a DoD test box.

NOT APPLICABLE — tenant binding, principal escalation, RBAC role mapping, token expiry, bearer tokens in URLs: this story mints no credential, reads none, and adds no principal-bearing surface. The one credential-adjacent statement (marker bytes never echoed, no credential material read or logged) is in the Observability Contract.
input-invariants: FIRED — 'Per-request size cap' and 'parser timeouts': both inherited rather than re-implemented — readBoxFile's byte cap and DEFAULT_PER_CALL_DEADLINE_MS, stated in Guards/limits as inherited bounds.

FIRED — 'Untrusted input parsed in isolation' / malformed-input fixture: /proc/uptime and the marker are box-supplied bytes on the trust boundary. The story routes both through the SAME four-kind classification and requires unparseable/absent uptime to be `uptime_unknown`, never silently floored to 'no reboot' — with a DoD test box. Round 2 additionally forced the numeric parse to be margin-guarded rather than raw-compared (AC4a), which is where the real input bug was.

FIRED — 'No path traversal' / server-derived key: the sweep derives every path from runId through the record store and run-lock's own assertValidRunId (run-lock.ts:937, validated BEFORE the path join), and adds no substrate command string under src/fleet/ (dispatch.ts:63-66 DoD) — the /proc/uptime read reuses readBoxFile precisely so no new sh -c string is minted.
NOT APPLICABLE — deserializer safety, MIME allowlist, archive expansion, served-content headers: no upload, no archive, no served path in this story.

cross_boundary_notes: DF3.7 EDIT REQUIRED (one clause, INV-IBOX-16) — the clause 'the observer is the only automatic caller of the host chain ... The invariant is no new automatic caller' is falsified by DF3.8, which is a second automatic caller by design. Proposed amendment, to be appended to INV-IBOX-16 rather than replacing it: 'DF3.8 adds the one further automatic caller this arc permits — a bounded, exiting `fleet observe` invocation — and pays for it by taking the per-run invocation lock this story declined to take, so the precondition strengthens from one caller by convention to one caller at a time by mutex. Any caller beyond those two reopens this invariant.' DF3.8 AC5 already states this from its side; leaving DF3.7 unedited leaves the two stories contradicting each other on the record.

DF3.7 EDIT REQUIRED (one clause, AC3) — AC3 cites 'the DF2.6 reaper's record-claim-refused arm (src/providers/reaper.ts:753) deliberately spares a box claimed by an open record'. That arm guards DESTROY only. An aged OPEN record classifies stale-record -> teardown (:480-487, :534-544) and is collected with harvest/destroy/revoke/closedAt and NO reverify(). The billing half of DF3.7's sentence is correct and should be left alone (sandbox-reap is dry-run unless --yes). Proposed amendment: after 'so the box bills until an operator acts on the typed refusal', add 'and when an operator does act via `sandbox-reap --yes` past staleAfterMs, the arm that fires is stale-record -> teardown, which collects the run without a witness and without ever reaching the gate — the failure DF3.8 exists to end.'

DF3.7 NON-EDIT, confirmed — INV-IBOX-14 and INV-IBOX-15 are inherited by DF3.8 verbatim; DF3.7's AC1 import fence is extended to src/fleet/observe.ts by the same grep test with no change to the fence itself; run-lock.ts is not among the four fenced modules, so the sweep taking a lock does not touch the fence.

DF3.7's verdict should be annotated rather than rewritten.

No edit is needed in DF1.10: its Trigger Surface already routes the gate/marker row to DF3.7, and its AC1 `fleet run <run-id>` is exactly the detachment mechanism DF3.8 AC7 cites.
